title: Platform Systems & Services: Runbooks, Dashboards, Alerts, and Roadmap
author: Morgan Lee
content:
Overview

This page consolidates platform engineering guidance for systems and services hosted by Redwood Inference. It includes: service inventory and ownership conventions, dashboard and alert standards, canonical runbooks and escalation flows, retrospective/run cadence, and a high-level roadmap for platform work. Use this as the single source of truth for operating platform services and for onboarding new platform engineers.

Scope

- Applies to: core platform services (control plane, routing, autoscaler, metric collection, logging, alerting, deployment pipelines), common infra components (k8s clusters, GPU pools), and shared observability artifacts.
- Not covered: product-specific application runbooks (owned by product teams) or customer-managed private deployments (see eng-private-deployments).

Owner and Contacts

- Platform Systems & Services: Platform Engineering team (oncall rotation)
- Primary contact: Morgan Lee (platform-systems@redwood.com)
- Ops pager: PagerDuty: Platform-Prod (escalation policy: primary -> secondary -> eng-lead)

Service Inventory and Ownership

Maintain a single inventory (CSV or Confluence table) listing service name, SLO class, primary owner, secondary owner, runbook link, dashboard link, and criticality. Example table (copy into page):

| Service | SLO Class | Primary Owner | Secondary Owner | Runbook | Dashboard | Criticality |
|---------|-----------|---------------|-----------------|---------|-----------|-------------|
| control-plane | gold (99.95% p99) | @morgan | @priya | /runbooks/control-plane | /dashboards/control-plane | P0 |
| inference-router | silver (99.9% p99) | @diego | @ethan | /runbooks/inference-router | /dashboards/inference-router | P0 |
| batch-queue | bronze (99% p95) | @sre-team | @infra | /runbooks/batch-queue | /dashboards/batch-queue | P2 |

SLOs and Error Budgets

- SLO classes: gold / silver / bronze. Each service must document an explicit SLA-derived SLO and the error budget policy (alert thresholds, rollback triggers).
- Example SLOs: gold = 99.95% p99 latency for API surface, silver = 99.9% p99, bronze = 99% p95.
- Error budget burn alerts: page-level alert when 25% used in 24h, team-level alert at 50% in 24h, exec-level at 80% in 7d.

Dashboards (Guidelines and Standards)

Every service must have a Grafana dashboard with the following panels at minimum:
1) Overview / health panel: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), CPU/GPU utilization, memory, queue depth.
2) Recent errors: top error types with sample traces/logs, 5xx traces count.
3) Capacity: instance counts, autoscaler activity, GPU memory pressure, batch worker backlog.
4) Dependency map: critical downstream services and their availability (upstream success rate).
5) SLO burn chart and error budget deficit.

Naming convention: dashboards are prefixed with "PLATFORM / <service-name> /" to make them discoverable in Grafana. Panels should include datasource links (Prometheus, Loki) and runbook links in the dashboard description.

Example Grafana panel query (Prometheus):
- p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-router"}[5m])) by (le))
- error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-router",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-router"}[5m]))

Alerts (Policy and Examples)

Alert design principles:
- Alert on user impact first (errors, latency SLO burn, throttling), then system impact (node memory pressure, disk full).
- Keep noise low: prefer composite alerts or multi-condition rules.
- Set severity tags (sev1, sev2, sev3) and map to PagerDuty escalation policies.

Suggested alert thresholds (adjust per service):
- Sev1: p99 latency > SLO threshold for 5m OR error rate > 1% absolute for 5m OR queue depth > 5x nominal
- Sev2: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10m OR disk > 90% on critical volumes OR GPU memory pressure > 80% for 10m
- Sev3: node restarts > 3 in 5m for non-critical nodes OR minor rate drops

Alert rule example (Prometheus YAML snippet):

- alert: InferenceRouter_P99Exceeded
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-router"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.9
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: sev1
    team: platform
  annotations:
    summary: "inference-router p99 latency > 900ms"
    runbook: "https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/inference-router"

Runbooks (Canonical Format)

Each runbook must follow a consistent structure so engineers can act quickly:
- Title, short description
- Owner and escalation contacts (PagerDuty, Slack channel)
- Preconditions and Impact (what does this affect)
- Observable symptoms (dashboard links, queries)
- Quick triage checklist (5 items max)
- Recovery steps (step-by-step with commands)
- Post-incident actions and links to postmortem template
- Test and verification steps
- RACI/ownership table

Sample quick triage checklist for high latency:
1) Check SLO burn & recent deploys (last 30 minutes)
2) Identify error type (5xx, timeouts, overloaded downstream)
3) Check autoscaler activity and pod counts
4) Check node/GPU utilization and OOM events
5) If capacity-constrained, initiate scale-up and open a mitigation PR

Sample recovery commands (k8s + infra):
- kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=inference-router -o wide
- kubectl logs -n platform <pod> -c router --since=15m
- kubectl exec -n platform <pod> -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep router'
- /opt/deploy/scripts/scale-cluster.sh --pool gpu-large --increase 2

Escalation Flow

1) Oncall (Platform primary) executes runbook. If unresolved in 15 minutes, escalate to Platform secondary.
2) If no progress in 30 minutes or customer-impacting, notify Engineering Lead and SRE Manager.
3) If incident meets sev1 criteria for >1 hour, open incident bridge, notify GTM and support, and create a postmortem.

Postmortems and Retrospectives

- All sev1 incidents require a postmortem within 72 hours draft and final within 14 days. Use the incident template under oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template.
- Retrospective cadence: Platform team runs a monthly operational retro focused on production incidents, pain points in dashboards/alerts, and one continuous improvement (CI) task to reduce toil.
- Retro output: action items with owners, estimated effort, and follow-up date tracked in the team wiki backlog.

Runbook Maintenance and Ownership

- Owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any prod incident affecting the service. Add a changelog entry at top of runbook with date and summary.
- When rotating oncall, the outgoing engineer must confirm all runbook links on the oncall checklist.

Operational Playbook: Day 0 / Day 1 / Day 2

- Day 0 (Design): Define SLO class, required metrics and dashboards, deploy smoke tests and synthetic checks.
- Day 1 (Launch): Enable alerts at conservative thresholds, validate dashboards, perform an operational readiness checklist, and add runbook.
- Day 2 (Run): Monitor error budget, tune alert thresholds to reduce noise, and schedule quarterly capacity reviews.

Platform Roadmap (next 6 quarters)

Q1-Q2 2026:
- Observability overhaul: migrate core dashboards to Grafana 9 dashboards with templating and folder structure.
- Controlled rollout of composite alerts to reduce paging noise by 40%.
- Launch SLO automation: auto-notifications for >25% budget burn.

Q3-Q4 2026:
- Autoscaler improvements for GPU pools (predictive scaling based on workload patterns).
- Unified service catalog with API and CI validation for runbook/dashboard presence.

2027 priorities:
- Advanced anomaly detection on metrics using ML-based baselines.
- Cross-team runbook exercises and biannual game days.

Team Wiki: Living Operational Knowledge

- The platform team wiki contains onboarding checklists, runbook templates, postmortem templates, standard Grafana/Prometheus snippets, and historical retros. Link important artifacts in the team handbook section: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026.

Onboarding checklist (new platform engineer):
1) Read this page and service inventory
2) Join PagerDuty and Slack channels (platform-prod, platform-alerts)
3) Access Grafana and Prometheus with SSO and visit 5 dashboards
4) Shadow oncall for one week and run one incident under supervision
5) Complete runbook update exercise for one owned service

Operational Exercises and Game Days

- Quarterly game day with a rotating scenario owner. Scenarios: sudden p99 spike, autoscaler failure, dependent DB outage, or capacity exhaustion. Document outcomes and action items in the team wiki.
